title: ARM Templates and Bicep

header.html: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources (20-25%)

Interpret an Azure Resource Manager template or a Bicep file; modify an existing template; modify an existing Bicep file; deploy resources by using a template or a Bicep file; export a deployment as a template or convert a template to a Bicep file
the official Microsoft Learn AZ-104 study guide, skills measured as of October 26, 2023

toc.title: Infrastructure as code with Azure Resource Manager

html:
1Infrastructure as code with Azure Resource Manager

Azure Resource Manager (ARM) is the management layer that handles every request to create, update or delete Azure resources (portal, CLI, PowerShell, SDKs all go through it).

An ARM template is a JSON file that declares the resources you want. Properties:

Property Meaning
Declarative You describe what you want, not the steps
Idempotent Deploying the same template repeatedly gives the same result
Repeatable The same template builds dev, test and production with different parameters

2Template structure

Section Purpose
$schema, contentVersion Required header
parameters Input values at deploy time (name, size, password)
variables Reusable values inside the template
resources The Azure resources to deploy
outputs Values returned after deployment (for example a connection string)

dependsOn makes one resource wait for another; ARM also infers dependencies from references. Template functions such as concat(), resourceGroup() and parameters() build values.

3Bicep

Bicep is a simpler language that compiles to ARM templates. It has cleaner syntax, automatic dependency handling, modules, and the same capabilities.

Topic Fact
Convert to Bicep az bicep decompile --file template.json turns an ARM template into Bicep
Convert to ARM az bicep build --file main.bicep produces the JSON
Parameters param location string = resourceGroup().location
Existing resource The existing keyword refers to a resource already deployed
Modules Split large deployments into reusable files
Exam tip

. Bicep and ARM templates are two ways to do the same thing; Bicep is the shorter one and compiles to ARM.

4Deploying

Item Detail
Commands az deployment group create (resource group scope), az deployment sub create, or PowerShell New-AzResourceGroupDeployment
Scopes Resource group, subscription, management group, tenant
Incremental mode (default) Adds or updates the resources in the template; leaves other resources alone
Complete mode Deletes resources in the resource group that are not in the template
What-if Previews changes before deploying
Parameter file A JSON file with values for the template parameters
Exam tip

. Complete mode can delete resources that are not in the template. Use what-if first.

5Exporting and modifying

Task How
Export a deployment as a template Portal: Automation > Export template on a resource group, a resource or a deployment
Modify Edit the JSON or Bicep (change a parameter default, SKU, location), then redeploy
Template spec Store a versioned template in Azure for others to deploy

Exported templates often need clean-up (some resources or secrets are not exported).

Exam tip

. Incremental mode (the default) never deletes; complete mode deletes resources that are not in the template.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which template section lets a user supply a VM name at deployment time?

  • Aparameters
  • Boutputs
  • Cvariables
  • Dresources
Show the answer

Answer: A. Parameters take input values at deployment.

S2A team deploys with complete mode and resources disappear. What happened?

  • AIncremental mode removed them because they were missing from the template
  • BAn Azure Policy assignment with a Delete effect removed them from the group
  • CA resource lock set to delete the resources that were not in the template
  • DComplete mode deleted resources in the resource group that were not in the template
Show the answer

Answer: D. Complete mode removes resources that are not in the template.

S3Which command converts an ARM template into Bicep?

  • Aaz bicep build
  • Baz deployment group create
  • Caz bicep decompile
  • Daz group delete
Show the answer

Answer: C. Decompile turns JSON into Bicep; build does the opposite.

S4An administrator wants to preview what a deployment would change before running it. What should be used?

  • AComplete mode
  • BA lock
  • CA tag
  • DWhat-if
Show the answer

Answer: D. What-if shows the planned changes.

S5What does it mean that ARM templates are idempotent?

  • ADeploying the same template repeatedly gives the same result
  • BThey can only be used once for each resource group in a subscription
  • CThey run on a schedule that is defined in the parameters section
  • DThey need no parameters because every value is fixed in the template
Show the answer

Answer: A. Repeated deployments produce the same state.

S6An administrator wants a template of an existing resource group to recreate it elsewhere. What can be used?

  • AAzure Advisor
  • BA budget
  • CSSPR
  • DExport template
Show the answer

Answer: D. Export template generates a template from existing resources.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What language is an ARM template written in?

Show the answer

JSON.

R2What does Bicep compile to?

Show the answer

An ARM template.

R3Which deployment mode is the default?

Show the answer

Incremental.

R4What is the outputs section for?

Show the answer

Returning values after deployment.

R5Name the template deployment scopes.

Show the answer

Resource group, subscription, management group and tenant.

R6What does a template spec store?

Show the answer

A versioned template for others to deploy.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
ARM template JSON; declarative, idempotent; parameters, variables, resources, outputs
Bicep simpler; compiles to ARM; decompile/build; modules
Deploy az deployment group create; incremental (default) vs complete; what-if
